periods.analysis: We open this cycle in a strong position: Part I Crime Rate is 28.6 per 1,000 residents, comfortably under the target of <=30. That result reflects steady incident coding from Patrol, the Airport District detail, and the Seaport Corridor burglary-suppression checks, with Records closing the quarter’s validation file on time. For Council, the main message is that Harborview is growing quickly, but the safety trend is being managed with disciplined deployment rather than one-time pushes.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping the weekly CompStat-lite review for the Waterfront, Northgate, and Airport District beats on the calendar through Q4. Ask Police Records to continue the 10-business-day quality check on Part I classifications so the next quarterly packet is clean and defensible. Extend the Seaport Corridor lighting-and-presence checklist to the three highest-call parking lots before holiday travel volume rises.

periods.analysis: Part I Crime Rate improved from 28.6 to 28.2 per 1,000 residents, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 0.4 and still green against the <=30 target. That movement is notable because Q4 brings holiday retail traffic at Harborview Commons, airport passenger surges, and more package-theft opportunities in the eastern neighborhoods. The departments did the quiet operational work well: retail liaison officers, port security coordination, and timely case reclassification all helped keep the number both lower and more reliable. We should give teams credit here while keeping the same reporting discipline that produced the result.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the holiday retail liaison model as a standing Q4 playbook, including the Harborview Commons, Old Wharf, and Central Avenue merchant routes. Continue monthly reconciliation between CAD calls, RMS entries, and final Part I coding so the 28.2 per 1,000 figure remains audit-ready. Before the next council update, add a one-page beat map showing where prevention activity was concentrated and where it should carry into Q1.

periods.analysis: The measure edged down again from 28.2 to 28.1 per 1,000 residents, a modest 0.1 improvement and another green quarter under the <=30 target. This is the kind of small but meaningful movement I like to see in a mature scorecard: not dramatic, but consistent, documented, and explainable. The winter pattern helped reduce some street activity, while targeted checks around the airport rental-car district and downtown garages helped prevent property-crime drift. Data quality remained solid, with no late reporting exception flagged for the quarterly close.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by keeping the Q1 garage-check protocol in place until daylight hours and visitor activity increase. Have Patrol and Community Safety jointly identify the top five repeat-location addresses from Q1 and assign a named follow-up owner for each before the Q2 reporting cutoff. Preserve the current Records review cadence, because the credibility of a 28.1 per 1,000 result depends on clean classification as much as field activity.

periods.analysis: Part I Crime Rate moved from 28.1 to 28.6 per 1,000 residents, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 0.5, but it remains green and below the <=30 target. The uptick is not surprising for Q2: warmer evenings, cruise and conference traffic through the seaport, and school-year transitions usually put more pressure on calls for service. The important management point is that the rate returned to the same level we saw in 2024-Q3, not above target, and the trend is still within the planned operating band. We should treat this as a friendly nudge to tighten summer readiness, not as a course change.
periods.recommendations: Activate the summer deployment checklist two weeks earlier, with foot and bike visibility on the Bayfront Promenade, Central Avenue, and the Route 17 transit spine. Add a Q2-to-Q3 watch item for theft-from-auto and commercial burglary so the next packet explains whether the 0.5 increase is seasonal or location-specific. Continue celebrating the green status, but pair it with a clear action owner for each hot spot so departments have what they need before peak visitor season.

periods.analysis: The rate increased from 28.6 to 29.2 per 1,000 residents, a quarter-over-quarter rise of 0.6, while still remaining green against the <=30 target. This is our closest point to the threshold so far in the arc, and it lines up with the busiest quarter for waterfront events, airport arrivals, and late-night activity around the stadium district. I would not overstate the concern, but I would not let the green color make us casual either. The good news is that analysts have enough clean location and time-of-day data to manage this before it becomes a council surprise.
periods.recommendations: Keep the objective green, but put a formal Q4 watch item on the stadium district, Bayfront Promenade, and airport hotel cluster. Direct the Crime Analysis Unit to produce a 30-day micro-hotspot list every Monday through October, with Patrol confirming visible follow-up by Friday. Sustain the prevention wins by extending merchant text alerts and garage signage beyond special events instead of treating them as temporary tools.

periods.analysis: This quarter shows a strong correction: Part I Crime Rate fell from 29.2 to 27.9 per 1,000 residents, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 1.3 and the best result in this series so far. The Q4 playbook appears to have worked, especially the Monday hotspot list, waterfront patrol overlap, and coordinated checks with airport and port security. This is a good example of why we track the objective quarterly: Q3 gave us an early nudge, and Q4 shows the organization responded. The result is green, credible, and a positive story for Council without pretending the work is finished.
periods.recommendations: Convert the Q4 hotspot process into a standing operating rhythm for 2026, not a one-quarter intervention. Ask Police, Airport Operations, and Port Security to document the shared patrol windows that supported the 27.9 per 1,000 result so they can be repeated during spring break and summer travel. Keep Records’ closeout deadline firm, with preliminary Part I validation completed five business days before the quarterly scorecard lock.

periods.analysis: The downward movement continued, with the rate improving from 27.9 to 27.6 per 1,000 residents, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 0.3 and another green result under the <=30 target. This is the lowest point in the eight-quarter arc to date, and it suggests the Q4 operating rhythm carried forward rather than fading after the holidays. Winter conditions likely helped, but the consistent follow-through on repeat locations and garage checks matters. For council framing, this is a disciplined safety story: a fast-growing city, a busy gateway economy, and a public safety system still holding the line.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the current CompStat-lite cadence and require each district captain to bring one prevention action tied to the prior month’s repeat-location list. Extend the airport hotel cluster partnership to include the new North Runway hospitality properties before Q2 occupancy increases. Keep the public narrative balanced: recognize the 27.6 per 1,000 result, then show the specific operating practices that will protect it.

periods.analysis: Part I Crime Rate rose from 27.6 to 29.4 per 1,000 residents, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 1.8, but the measure remains green and below the <=30 target. This is the sharpest increase in the series and brings us close enough to the threshold that we need a clear, deadline-aware response before Q3 peak season. The pattern is plausibly tied to early summer visitor volume, vehicle break-ins near waterfront lots, and more activity along the Route 17 and Route 22 corridors. The status is still green, but this is a watchful green: departments have earned confidence, and now they need the same organized follow-through that corrected 2025-Q3.
periods.recommendations: Launch a 45-day summer stabilization sprint focused on waterfront lots W-3, W-5, and W-8, the Route 17/22 transfer points, and the airport hotel cluster. Have Crime Analysis separate violent, property, and auto-related Part I drivers before the next reporting lock so Council sees what is actually moving the 29.4 per 1,000 result. Sustain the proven Q4/Q1 practices, but extend visible patrol windows to Thursday-Sunday evenings through Labor Day. Put an interim check-in on the executive agenda by mid-quarter so we do not wait for the next scorecard cycle to adjust.

periods.analysis: The crime rate eased to 30.9 per 1,000 from 31.2, but remains above the target of 28. The improvement is not yet enough to close the public-safety gap.
periods.recommendations: Review the previously identified theft and burglary locations and bring the next deployment decision to the executive check-in.
